1.15.title: Disorders of the skeletal spine resulting in compromise of a nerve root(s)
1.15.summary: Spine disorder compressing a nerve root, with radicular symptoms, neurological signs on exam or electrodiagnostic testing, imaging confirmation in cervical or lumbosacral spine, and ≥12-month physical limitation requiring an assistive device or producing inability to use upper extremities.

children.criterion: Radicular distribution of symptoms consistent with nerve root compromise
Pain in radicular distribution consistent with nerve root compromise
Paresthesia in radicular distribution consistent with nerve root compromise
Muscle fatigue in radicular distribution consistent with nerve root compromise
Radicular neurological signs on physical examination or diagnostic test
Muscle weakness in a myotomal pattern documented on physical examination
Signs of nerve root irritation, tension, or compression on physical exam (e.g., positive straight leg raise, Spurling, Lasegue)
Sensory changes OR decreased deep tendon reflexes
Decreased sensation in radicular distribution on physical exam
Abnormal sensory nerve latency on electrodiagnostic testing (EMG/NCS)
Decreased deep tendon reflexes in radicular distribution
Imaging findings consistent with nerve root compromise in cervical or lumbosacral spine (e.g., disc herniation, foraminal stenosis on MRI/CT/myelogram)
Physical limitation lasting ≥12 months with documented assistive device need OR upper extremity inability
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Documented medical need for two-handed assistive device OR limitation of one or both upper extremities
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device
Inability to use one upper extremity for fine and gross movements; needs one-handed assistive device requiring the other upper extremity
Inability to use either upper extremity for fine and gross movements (work-related activities)

1.16.title: Lumbar spinal stenosis resulting in compromise of the cauda equina
1.16.summary: Lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication or sensorimotor signs, imaging-confirmed cauda equina compromise, and ≥12-month limitation requiring two-handed assistive device.

children.criterion: Symptoms of neurogenic claudication, including nonradicular pain in lower back/buttocks/thighs and/or nonradicular sensory loss
Nonradicular neurological signs on examination
Muscle weakness on physical examination of lower extremities
Sensory changes OR decreased deep tendon reflexes
Decreased sensation in lower extremities on physical exam
Abnormal sensory nerve latency on electrodiagnostic testing
Areflexia or hyporeflexia of lower extremities
Findings on imaging or operative report consistent with compromise of cauda equina with lumbar spinal stenosis
Physical limitation lasting ≥12 months with documented assistive device need
Impairment-related physical limitation lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device

1.17.title: Reconstructive surgery or surgical arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint
1.17.summary: Reconstructive surgery or arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint with impairment-related limitation lasting ≥12 months and documented need for two-handed assistive device.

children.criterion: Surgical reconstruction or arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint (hip, knee, ankle, or ankle-hindfoot complex)
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, ≥12 months from the surgery
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device

1.18.title: Abnormality of a major joint(s) in any extremity
1.18.summary: Major joint abnormality with chronic pain or stiffness, abnormal motion or instability, imaging confirmation of joint abnormality, and ≥12-month limitation requiring assistive device or producing inability to use upper extremities.

children.criterion: Chronic joint pain or stiffness in a major joint
Abnormal motion, instability, or immobility on physical examination of the joint
Imaging or other findings of joint abnormality (joint space narrowing, bony destruction, ankylosis, instability)
Physical limitation lasting ≥12 months with documented assistive device need OR upper extremity inability
Impairment-related physical limitation lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Documented two-handed assistive device need OR upper extremity limitation
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device
Inability to use one upper extremity for fine and gross movements; needs one-handed assistive device requiring the other upper extremity
Inability to use either upper extremity for fine and gross movements

1.19.title: Pathologic fractures due to any cause
1.19.summary: Three pathologic fractures within a 12-month period from a disorder weakening bone (osteoporosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, etc.), with limitation requiring assistive device or producing inability to use upper extremities.

children.criterion: Three pathologic fractures occurring on separate, distinct occasions within any 12-month period
Underlying disorder that weakens bone (osteoporosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, skeletal dysplasia, medication side effect, endocrine disorder)
Documented assistive device need OR upper extremity inability
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device
Inability to use one upper extremity for fine and gross movements; needs one-handed assistive device requiring the other upper extremity
Inability to use either upper extremity for fine and gross movements

1.20.title: Amputation due to any cause
1.20.summary: Amputation that meets one of four scenarios: both upper extremities, hemipelvectomy/hip disarticulation, lower extremity at/above ankle precluding effective ambulation, or one hand and one lower extremity precluding effective ambulation.

children.criterion: Amputation of both upper extremities at or above the wrist
Hemipelvectomy or hip disarticulation
Amputation of one or both lower extremities at or above the ankle, with stump complications precluding effective prosthetic use, lasting ≥12 months
Amputation of one or both lower extremities at or above the ankle
Stump complications (non-healing wounds, ulceration, instability) preventing or precluding effective prosthetic use
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device
Amputation of one hand AND one lower extremity at or above the ankle, with two-handed assistive device need lasting ≥12 months
Amputation of one upper extremity at or above the wrist AND one lower extremity at or above the ankle
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device, lasting ≥12 months

1.21.title: Soft tissue injury or abnormality under continuing surgical management
1.21.summary: Soft tissue injury (including burns) under continuing surgical management directed at saving, reconstructing, or replacing the affected part, with continuing management expected to last ≥12 months and maximum benefit from therapy not yet achieved.

children.criterion: Soft tissue injury or abnormality of an extremity, trunk, or face/head requiring continuing surgical management
Continuing surgical management directed at saving, reconstructing, or replacing the affected body part
Continuing surgical management expected to last, or has lasted, ≥12 months from initial event, with maximum benefit from therapy not yet achieved

1.22.title: Non-healing or complex fracture of the femur, tibia, pelvis, or one or more of the tarsal bones
1.22.summary: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of femur, tibia, pelvis, or tarsal bones, imaging-confirmed, with limitation lasting ≥12 months and need for two-handed assistive device.

children.criterion: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of femur, tibia, pelvis, or one or more tarsal bones
Imaging documenting the non-healing or complex nature of the fracture
≥12-month physical limitation with documented two-handed assistive device need
Impairment-related physical limitation lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device

1.23.title: Non-healing or complex fracture of an upper extremity
1.23.summary: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of upper extremity (humerus, radius, ulna), imaging-confirmed, with ≥12-month inability to use both upper extremities for fine and gross movements.

children.criterion: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of an upper extremity (humerus, radius, ulna)
Imaging documenting the non-healing or complex nature of the fracture
≥12-month inability to use both upper extremities for fine and gross movements
Impairment-related limitation lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Inability to use both upper extremities for fine and gross movements (work-related activities)

2.02.title: Loss of central visual acuity
2.02.summary: Best-corrected central visual acuity in the better eye of 20/200 or worse.

rule_json.criterion: Best-corrected central visual acuity in the better eye of 20/200 or worse, measured by ophthalmologist or optometrist

2.03.title: Contraction of the visual field in the better eye
2.03.summary: Contraction of visual field in the better eye meeting one of: widest diameter ≤20°, mean deviation worse than -22 dB, or visual field efficiency ≤20%.

children.criterion: Widest diameter of visual field in the better eye, subtending an angle around the point of fixation, no greater than 20°
Mean deviation (MD) of -22 dB or worse in the better eye on automated static threshold perimetry (HFA)
Visual field efficiency of 20% or less in the better eye

2.04.title: Visual impairment (combined acuity and field impairment)
2.04.summary: Visual impairment value of 1.00 or greater in the better eye, calculated by adding visual acuity impairment value and visual field impairment value.

rule_json.criterion: Visual impairment value of 1.00 or greater in the better eye (sum of visual acuity impairment value and visual field impairment value calculated per SSA formula)

2.07.title: Disturbance of labyrinthine-vestibular function
2.07.summary: Disturbance of labyrinthine-vestibular function with disturbed equilibrium AND hearing impairment, all confirmed by appropriate tests.

children.criterion: History of frequent attacks of balance disturbance, tinnitus, and progressive hearing loss
Disturbed function of vestibular labyrinth demonstrated by caloric or other vestibular tests
Hearing loss established by audiometry

2.09.title: Loss of speech
2.09.summary: Loss of speech due to any cause, with inability to produce by any means speech that can be heard, understood, or sustained.

rule_json.criterion: Loss of speech due to any cause, with inability to produce — by any means — speech that can be heard, understood, or sustained

2.10.title: Hearing loss not treated with cochlear implantation
2.10.summary: Hearing loss in the better ear meeting one of: pure-tone average ≥90 dB AND bone conduction average ≥60 dB, OR word recognition score 40% or less.

children.criterion: Average air conduction hearing threshold of 90 decibels (dB) or greater in the better ear AND average bone conduction hearing threshold of 60 dB or greater in the better ear (at 500, 1000, and 2000 Hz)
Word recognition score of 40% or less in the better ear, determined using a standardized list of phonetically balanced monosyllabic words

2.11.title: Hearing loss treated with cochlear implantation
2.11.summary: Hearing loss treated with cochlear implantation; considered disabled for 1 year following implantation, after which evaluation is based on word recognition score on HINT (≤60% qualifies).

children.criterion: Within 1 year of cochlear implantation surgery (claimant considered disabled for 1 year)
After 1 year, word recognition score of 60% or less determined by HINT (Hearing in Noise Test)

3.02.title: Chronic respiratory disorders
3.02.summary: Chronic respiratory disorder (COPD, emphysema, pulmonary fibrosis, pneumoconiosis, bronchiectasis) meeting one of: low FEV1, low FVC, low DLCO, low ABG/SpO2, or three exacerbations within 12 months requiring hospitalization.

children.criterion: FEV1 less than or equal to the value in SSA Table I-A or I-B for age, sex, and height (without shoes), measured during stable period
FVC less than or equal to the value in SSA Table II-A or II-B for age, sex, and height (without shoes)
Chronic impairment of gas exchange demonstrated by DLCO ≤ Table III value, or arterial PaO2/PaCO2 ≤ Table IV-A/B/C, or SpO2 ≤ Table V on pulse oximetry
Three exacerbations or complications within 12-month period, each lasting ≥48 hours and requiring hospitalization, with at least 30 days between each
Three separate hospitalizations for respiratory exacerbations or complications within a consecutive 12-month period
Each hospitalization lasted at least 48 hours, with at least 30 days between consecutive hospitalizations

3.03.title: Asthma
3.03.summary: Asthma with low FEV1 at baseline AND three asthma exacerbations within a 12-month period requiring hospitalization for ≥48 hours, despite prescribed treatment.

children.criterion: Baseline FEV1 less than or equal to the value in SSA Table VI-A or VI-B for age, sex, and height, measured while medically stable, within the same 12-month period as required hospitalizations

Three asthma exacerbations within a consecutive 12-month period requiring hospitalization for at least 48 hours each, with at least 30 days between consecutive hospitalizations, despite adherence to prescribed treatment

3.04.title: Cystic fibrosis
3.04.summary: Cystic fibrosis (genetic/sweat test confirmed) meeting one of: low FEV1, exacerbations requiring hospitalization, low SpO2, hemoptysis, pulmonary hypertension, weight loss, or respiratory failure.

children.criterion: Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis by sweat chloride test or genetic testing for CFTR mutations
One of: low FEV1, exacerbations, low oxygenation, hemoptysis, pulmonary HTN, weight loss, or respiratory failure
FEV1 ≤ value in SSA Table VII-A or VII-B for age, sex, and height
Two or more pulmonary exacerbations in 12 months requiring IV antibiotics, IV chest physiotherapy, or hospitalization
SpO2 ≤ value in Table VIII on pulse oximetry while breathing room air at rest, or after 6-minute walk
Hemoptysis (other than blood-streaked sputum) requiring vascular embolization to control bleeding
Pulmonary hypertension confirmed by mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥25 mm Hg on right heart catheterization
Respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, noninvasive ventilation with BiPAP, or a combination of both for ≥48 consecutive hours, occurring twice within 12 months
Weight loss with low BMI: BMI ≤18 (adults) or weight loss with documented poor nutritional status

3.07.title: Bronchiectasis
3.07.summary: Bronchiectasis (imaging-confirmed) with three exacerbations within 12 months requiring hospitalization for ≥48 hours each, with at least 30 days between hospitalizations.

children.criterion: Bronchiectasis documented by imaging (high-resolution CT preferred)
Three exacerbations or complications within 12 months, each requiring hospitalization for ≥48 hours, with at least 30 days between consecutive hospitalizations

3.09.title: Chronic pulmonary hypertension due to any cause
3.09.summary: Chronic pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization showing mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥40 mm Hg.

rule_json.criterion: Chronic pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization showing mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥40 mm Hg

3.11.title: Lung transplantation
3.11.summary: Lung transplantation (single or bilateral); claimant considered disabled for 3 years post-transplant.

children.criterion: Lung transplantation (single or bilateral) documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 3 years of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 3 years post-transplant)

3.14.title: Respiratory failure
3.14.summary: Respiratory failure due to chronic respiratory disorder requiring invasive mechanical ventilation or noninvasive ventilation with BiPAP for ≥48 consecutive hours, twice within 12 months with at least 30 days between events.

children.criterion: Respiratory failure due to chronic respiratory disorder
Two episodes of respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation or BiPAP for ≥48 consecutive hours, occurring within a 12-month period with at least 30 days between events

4.02.title: Chronic heart failure
4.02.summary: Chronic heart failure (systolic or diastolic) with documented ventricular dysfunction by echocardiogram or other testing, persistent symptoms despite treatment, plus inability to perform exercise testing safely OR three episodes of heart failure within 12 months.

children.criterion: Documented chronic heart failure (systolic or diastolic) on imaging while medically stable: ejection fraction ≤30% during stable period, OR diastolic dysfunction with LV posterior wall + septum ≥2.5 cm and enlarged left atrium
Persistent symptoms of heart failure that very seriously limit ability to do activities of daily living
Inability to perform exercise tolerance test OR three episodes of heart failure
Inability to perform exercise tolerance test at workload equivalent to 5 METs or less due to symptoms (chest discomfort, dyspnea, fatigue, ischemic ECG changes, arrhythmia, BP drop)
Three or more separate episodes of acute heart failure within 12 months requiring emergency department or hospital treatment, with intervening period of stability
Inability to perform exercise tolerance test at workload of 5 METs because exercise testing would present significant risk to the individual

4.04.title: Ischemic heart disease
4.04.summary: Ischemic heart disease with chest discomfort due to myocardial ischemia, plus one of: positive exercise tolerance test at low workload, three ischemic episodes within 12 months requiring revascularization, or coronary angiography showing significant disease.

children.criterion: Symptoms due to myocardial ischemia (typical angina, atypical angina, or anginal equivalent) while on prescribed treatment
One of: ETT findings, three ischemic episodes, or significant coronary disease on angiography
Sign- or symptom-limited exercise tolerance test demonstrating ischemic findings (ST depression ≥1 mm in non-leads, decrease in BP, abnormal radionuclide uptake) at workload equivalent to ≤5 METs
Three separate ischemic episodes requiring revascularization or unsuccessful revascularization within 12 months

Coronary angiography showing 50% or greater stenosis of left main coronary artery, or 70% or greater stenosis of another non-bypassed coronary artery, or 50% or greater stenosis of a bypass graft, with very serious limitation of ADLs

4.05.title: Recurrent arrhythmias
4.05.summary: Recurrent arrhythmias (not due to reversible cause) with uncontrolled syncope or near-syncope, despite prescribed treatment, with documented arrhythmia coincident with symptoms by ECG or Holter monitor.

children.criterion: Recurrent arrhythmias not related to reversible cause (electrolyte abnormality, thyroid dysfunction, drug effect)
Uncontrolled recurrent episodes of syncope or near-syncope despite adherence to prescribed treatment
Documentation by ECG, ambulatory monitoring (Holter), or other appropriate testing showing arrhythmia coincident with the syncope or near-syncope

4.06.title: Symptomatic congenital heart disease
4.06.summary: Symptomatic congenital heart disease with one of: cyanosis at rest, intermittent right-to-left shunting with hypoxemia, or secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

children.criterion: Documented symptomatic congenital heart disease
One of: cyanosis at rest, hypoxemic spells, or pulmonary vascular disease
Cyanosis at rest with hematocrit ≥55% on two evaluations 3+ months apart in a 12-month period, or arterial PaO2 ≤60 mm Hg at altitude <3000 feet
Intermittent right-to-left shunting with hypoxemia at rest or with exercise
Secondary pulmonary vascular disease with mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥40 mm Hg

4.09.title: Heart transplant
4.09.summary: Heart transplantation; claimant considered disabled for 1 year following surgery; afterward evaluated under residual impairment.

children.criterion: Heart transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

4.10.title: Aneurysm of aorta or major branches
4.10.summary: Aortic aneurysm or aneurysm of major branches with dissection not controlled by treatment, demonstrated by appropriate imaging.

children.criterion: Aneurysm of the aorta or major branches with dissection
Dissection not controlled by prescribed treatment, demonstrated by imaging

4.11.title: Chronic venous insufficiency
4.11.summary: Chronic venous insufficiency of a lower extremity with extensive brawny edema or superficial varicosities, stasis dermatitis, and recurrent or persistent ulceration not healing after 3 months of prescribed treatment.

children.criterion: Chronic venous insufficiency of a lower extremity with deep venous thrombosis, valvular incompetence, or post-thrombotic syndrome

Extensive brawny edema involving at least two-thirds of the leg between ankle and knee, OR superficial varicosities, stasis dermatitis, AND recurrent or persistent ulceration that has not healed after at least 3 months of prescribed treatment

4.12.title: Peripheral arterial disease
4.12.summary: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) with intermittent claudication and one of: significantly reduced ankle-brachial systolic pressure ratio, low resting toe systolic pressure, or low resting toe-brachial pressure ratio.

children.criterion: Peripheral arterial disease as determined by appropriate medically acceptable imaging or testing, with intermittent claudication
One of: low ABI, low resting toe pressure, low toe-brachial ratio, or exercise testing with significant drop
Resting ankle-brachial systolic pressure ratio (ABI) less than 0.50
Resting toe systolic pressure less than 30 mm Hg
Resting toe-brachial pressure ratio less than 0.40
Resting systolic blood pressure in ankle ≤50% of systolic BP at peripheral arterial site, with exercise drop

5.02.title: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging from any cause
5.02.summary: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging from any cause requiring blood transfusion of at least 2 units of blood per transfusion on at least three occasions during a consecutive 6-month period, with at least 30 days between hospitalizations.

children.criterion: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging from any cause
Required blood transfusion of at least 2 units per transfusion, on at least three occasions during a consecutive 6-month period

5.05.title: Chronic liver disease
5.05.summary: Chronic liver disease meeting one of: hemorrhaging from varices/portal hypertensive gastropathy, ascites/hydrothorax, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatopulmonary syndrome, hepatic encephalopathy, or end-stage liver disease (high MELD).

children.criterion: Hemorrhaging from esophageal, gastric, or ectopic varices or portal hypertensive gastropathy with hemodynamic instability requiring transfusion of at least 2 units of blood
Ascites or hydrothorax not attributable to other causes, present despite continuing treatment
Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) with peritoneal fluid containing absolute neutrophil count of at least 250 cells/mm³
Hepatorenal syndrome documented by elevated serum creatinine, oliguria, and absence of other causes of renal failure
Hepatopulmonary syndrome documented by arterial hypoxemia and intrapulmonary vascular dilatations
Hepatic encephalopathy documented by altered mental status with elevated ammonia or asterixis
End-stage liver disease with MELD score of 22 or greater on at least 2 evaluations within a 6-month period

5.06.title: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
5.06.summary: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's or ulcerative colitis) with obstruction requiring hospitalization, OR two of the following within 6 months: anemia, low albumin, tender abdominal mass, perineal disease, weight loss, or dependence on supplemental daily nutrition.

children.criterion: Obstruction of stenotic areas (not adhesions) in small intestine or colon with proximal dilation, confirmed by imaging or in surgery, requiring hospitalization for intestinal decompression or surgery on two occasions within consecutive 6-month period
Two of the following despite continuing treatment, present on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a 6-month period
At least two of the listed symptoms
Anemia with hemoglobin <10.0 g/dL
Serum albumin ≤3.0 g/dL
Clinically documented tender abdominal mass with abdominal pain or cramping not controlled by prescribed narcotic medication
Perineal disease with draining abscess or fistula with pain
Involuntary weight loss of at least 10% from baseline
Need for supplemental daily enteral nutrition via gastrostomy or daily parenteral nutrition via central venous catheter
On at least two evaluations 60 days apart in 6-month period

5.07.title: Intestinal failure
5.07.summary: Intestinal failure due to short bowel syndrome, chronic motility disorders, or extensive small bowel mucosal disease, resulting in dependence on daily parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter for at least 12 months.

children.criterion: Intestinal failure due to one of three underlying conditions
Short bowel syndrome
Chronic motility disorder
Extensive small bowel mucosal disease
Dependence on daily parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter
Parenteral nutrition dependence lasting at least 12 months

5.08.title: Weight loss due to any digestive disorder
5.08.summary: Documented weight loss due to any digestive disorder, with BMI ≤17.50 calculated on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a consecutive 6-month period, despite continuing treatment.

children.criterion: Documented digestive disorder causing weight loss
BMI ≤17.50 on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a consecutive 6-month period, despite continuing treatment

5.09.title: Liver transplantation
5.09.summary: Liver transplantation; considered disabled for 1 year following the date of transplantation, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Liver transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

5.11.title: Small intestine transplantation
5.11.summary: Small intestine transplantation; considered disabled for 1 year from the date of transplant, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Small intestine transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

5.12.title: Pancreas transplantation
5.12.summary: Pancreas transplantation; considered disabled for 1 year from the date of transplant, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Pancreas transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

6.03.title: Chronic kidney disease with chronic hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis
6.03.summary: Chronic kidney disease requiring chronic hemodialysis OR chronic peritoneal dialysis, lasting or expected to last for at least 12 continuous months.

children.criterion: Chronic kidney disease diagnosis
Chronic dialysis via one of two equivalent modalities
Chronic hemodialysis
Chronic peritoneal dialysis
Dialysis lasting or expected to last 12 continuous months

6.04.title: Chronic kidney disease with kidney transplant
6.04.summary: Chronic kidney disease with kidney transplantation; claimant considered disabled for 1 year following the date of transplant, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Kidney transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

6.05.title: Chronic kidney disease with impairment of kidney function
6.05.summary: Chronic kidney disease with both: (A) reduced glomerular filtration evidenced by elevated serum creatinine, low creatinine clearance, or low eGFR on at least two occasions 90+ days apart within 12 months, AND (B) one of four complications: renal osteodystrophy with bone pain + imaging, peripheral neuropathy, fluid overload syndrome, or anorexia with BMI <=18.0.

children.criterion: Reduced glomerular filtration: one of three lab findings on at least two occasions at least 90 days apart within a consecutive 12-month period
Serum creatinine of 4 mg/dL or greater
Creatinine clearance of 20 mL/min or less
Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 20 mL/min/1.73m^2 or less
One of four complications of CKD
Renal osteodystrophy with severe bone pain AND imaging studies documenting bone abnormalities (osteitis fibrosa, osteomalacia, or pathologic fractures)
Peripheral neuropathy (uremic or other)
Fluid overload syndrome documented by one of two findings
Diastolic hypertension >=110 mmHg despite at least 90 consecutive days of prescribed therapy, documented by at least two measurements at least 90 days apart within a 12-month period
Signs of vascular congestion or anasarca despite at least 90 consecutive days of prescribed therapy, documented on at least two occasions at least 90 days apart within a 12-month period
Anorexia with weight loss determined by body mass index (BMI) of 18.0 or less, calculated on at least two occasions at least 90 days apart within a 12-month period

6.06.title: Nephrotic syndrome
6.06.summary: Nephrotic syndrome with laboratory findings of heavy proteinuria (either >=10 g/24h OR >=3.5 g/24h with low serum albumin), AND anasarca persisting at least 90 days despite prescribed treatment.

children.criterion: Laboratory findings supporting nephrotic syndrome, documented on at least two occasions >=90 days apart within a 12-month period
Proteinuria of 10.0 g or greater per 24 hours
Serum albumin <=3.0 g/dL with proteinuria >=3.5 g/24h or UPCR >=3.5
Serum albumin of 3.0 g/dL or less
Heavy urinary protein loss
Proteinuria of 3.5 g or greater per 24 hours
Urine total-protein-to-creatinine ratio of 3.5 or greater
Anasarca persisting for at least 90 days despite prescribed treatment

6.09.title: Complications of chronic kidney disease
6.09.summary: Chronic kidney disease (not requiring chronic dialysis) with three hospitalizations within a 12-month period for CKD complications, each lasting at least 48 hours, occurring at least 30 days apart.

children.criterion: Chronic kidney disease (not requiring chronic dialysis)

At least three hospitalizations within a consecutive 12-month period for CKD complications, occurring at least 30 days apart, with each hospitalization lasting at least 48 hours (including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization)

7.05.title: Hemolytic anemias, including sickle cell disease, thalassemia, and their variants
7.05.summary: Hemolytic anemia (sickle cell disease, thalassemia, etc.) with documented severe complications (vaso-occlusive crises, transfusion needs, hemolytic crises) occurring at specified frequency within 12-month period.

children.criterion: Documented painful (vaso-occlusive) crises requiring parenteral narcotic medication occurring at least 6 times within 12-month period, with at least 30 days between crises
Hospital complications occurring at least 3 times within 12-month period (hospital admission lasting ≥48 hours; each at least 30 days apart)
Chronic, severe anemia with hemoglobin ≤7.0 g/dL on at least 3 evaluations at least 30 days apart within 12-month period
Beta thalassemia major requiring life-long red blood cell transfusions at least once every 6 weeks to maintain Hgb

7.08.title: Disorders of thrombosis and hemostasis
7.08.summary: Thrombotic or coagulation disorder with complications requiring at least three hospitalizations within 12-month period, each lasting ≥48 hours and at least 30 days apart.

children.criterion: Disorder of thrombosis or hemostasis (hemophilia, von Willebrand disease, recurrent thromboembolism, etc.)
Three hospitalizations within 12-month period for complications of the disorder (bleeding episodes, thrombotic events), each lasting ≥48 hours, at least 30 days apart

7.10.title: Disorders of bone marrow failure
7.10.summary: Bone marrow failure (aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic syndrome, etc.) with severe infection or bleeding requiring hospitalizations, OR transfusion-dependence, OR severe cytopenias.

children.criterion: Hospitalization for complications (severe infection or hemorrhage) requiring ≥48-hour hospitalization, occurring at least three times within 12-month period
Transfusion-dependent severe anemia (Hgb ≤7.0) on at least 3 occasions in 12 months, OR thrombocytopenia (PLT ≤30,000) on at least 3 evaluations 30+ days apart in 12 months

7.17.title: Hematological disorders treated by bone marrow or stem cell transplantation
7.17.summary: Bone marrow or stem cell transplantation for hematological disorder; considered disabled for 12 months from date of transplantation, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Bone marrow or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for a hematological disorder
Within 12 months of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 12 months post-transplant)

7.18.title: Repeated complications of hematological disorders
7.18.summary: Hematological disorder with repeated complications resulting in significant interference with ADLs, social functioning, or completing tasks in timely manner due to deficiencies in concentration/persistence/pace.

children.criterion: Documented hematological disorder with repeated complications (despite continuing treatment)
At least two constitutional symptoms (severe fatigue, fever, malaise, weight loss)
Marked limitation in ADLs, social functioning, or completing tasks in timely manner
Marked limitation in activities of daily living
Marked limitation in social functioning
Marked limitation in completing tasks in timely manner due to concentration, persistence, or pace deficiencies

8.02.title: Ichthyosis
8.02.summary: Ichthyosis with extensive skin lesions persisting at least 3 months despite continuing treatment.

children.criterion: Ichthyosis with extensive skin lesions involving multiple body sites (palms, soles, both axillae, both inguinal areas, perineum, etc.)
Persistent for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment

8.03.title: Bullous disease
8.03.summary: Bullous disease (pemphigus, bullous pemphigoid, dermatitis herpetiformis, epidermolysis bullosa) with extensive skin lesions persisting at least 3 months despite continuing treatment.

children.criterion: Bullous disease with extensive skin lesions
Persistent for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment

8.04.title: Chronic infections of the skin or mucous membranes
8.04.summary: Chronic infection of skin or mucous membranes with extensive fungating or extensive ulcerating lesions, persisting at least 3 months despite continuing treatment.

children.criterion: Chronic infection of skin or mucous membranes with extensive fungating or extensive ulcerating lesions
Persistent for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment

8.05.title: Dermatitis
8.05.summary: Dermatitis (psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis) with extensive skin lesions persisting at least 3 months despite continuing treatment.

children.criterion: Dermatitis with extensive skin lesions involving multiple body sites
